nodes.name: Wrist preparation

form: Full weight through the palm with fingers actively gripping
No pain at the front of the joint — pressure is fine, pinching is not
Completed in all four positions: flexion, extension, and both rotations

nodes.note: Ayalon's non-negotiable. Wrists are the tissue that caps handstand volume, and they adapt far slower than the shoulders that want the work.

nodes.name: Hollow body hold

form: Lower back stays flat against the floor for the whole hold
Shoulders and feet both off the floor
Breathing continues — a hold you cannot breathe through is a brace, not a position

nodes.note: The handstand line is a vertical hollow. Learn it on the floor where you can see it fail.

form: Shoulders stacked directly over hands
Ribs down, no arch through the lower back
Elbows locked

nodes.name: Chest-to-wall handstand

form: Only the toes touch the wall — nothing else rests on it
Full shoulder elevation, ears covered by the arms
Straight line from hands through hips to heels

nodes.note: This is the position. Everything after it is about removing the wall, not about changing the shape.

form: Arrives in balance without crashing into the wall
Same leg leads every repetition
Steps down under control rather than falling out
No wall contact at any point
Balance corrected through the fingers, not by piking at the hips
Exits on the athlete's terms

nodes.name: Freestanding handstand — 30 seconds

form: No wall contact
Straight line held throughout — a banana handstand held for 30 seconds is a different skill
Controlled exit

nodes.note: Thirty unbroken seconds is the point at which the handstand stops being a balance trick and becomes a position you can work from.

nodes.name: Strict pull-up × 10

form: Dead hang at the bottom, elbows fully extended
Chin clearly over the bar
No kip, no leg drive

nodes.note: Vadnal's entry standard. Below ten strict, the muscle-up is a strength problem wearing a technique costume.

nodes.name: Straight-bar dip × 8

form: Shoulders descend below the elbows
Bar stays in contact with the torso through the bottom
Locked out at the top without shrugging

nodes.note: Straight bar, not rings or parallels. The muscle-up catch happens on a bar and the wrist position is the hard part.

form: Sternum makes contact with the bar
Bottom of every rep is a full dead hang
Torso stays close to vertical

nodes.name: Sternum pull-up × 3

form: Bar reaches the bottom of the sternum or lower
Elbows drive back and down
Strict — no hip drive

nodes.note: The height test. If the bar cannot reach low ribs, there is nothing to transition from.

nodes.name: Assisted transition × 5

form: Passes through the transition slowly rather than being thrown through it
Wrists rotate over the bar deliberately
No shoulder pain at any point in the rotation

nodes.note: Dunham's point: the transition is a separate skill from both the pull and the dip, and it is the one nobody trains.

form: Starts from a dead hang
No kip and no leg swing
Finishes at a full lockout above the bar
Three consecutive from a dead hang
Strict throughout — the third rep is where the kip creeps in
Controlled descent on every rep

nodes.name: Scapular pull-up × 10

form: Elbows stay completely straight
Movement comes from the shoulder blades alone
Slow and controlled in both directions

nodes.note: Ladon's foundation. The front lever is a straight-arm strength skill, and straight-arm strength is trained here or not at all.

form: Lower back flat throughout
Legs straight and together
Breathing continues
Torso horizontal — hips at shoulder height, not below
Arms completely straight
Scapulae protracted and depressed, not shrugged
Back flat and parallel to the floor
Thighs perpendicular to the torso, knees roughly at 90°
No sag at the hips
Extended leg fully straight
Hips level — no rotation toward the tucked side
Body horizontal
Both legs straight and level with the torso
Horizontal line from shoulders to hips
Arms locked
Legs together and straight
Whole body horizontal — hips do not drop below shoulders
Held, not passed through

nodes.name: Seated compression lifts × 10

form: Legs straight, lifted from the floor by the hip flexors alone
Torso stays upright — no leaning back to cheat the lift
Held for a beat at the top of each rep

nodes.note: Liu's insight: most failed L-sits are a compression problem, not a triceps or shoulder problem. Train the thing that is actually missing.

form: Elbows locked
Shoulders depressed — actively pushed away from the ears
Hips under, not behind, the shoulders
Heels resting lightly, taking minimal weight
Legs straight
Shoulders stay depressed for the whole hold
Knees lifted to at least hip height
Elbows locked, shoulders depressed
No rocking backwards to hold the position
Extended leg straight and at least parallel to the floor
Hips square
Both sides trained equally
Both legs straight and at or above parallel
Knees locked
Shoulders depressed and elbows locked for the whole hold
